title: Spartan Women
objective: After this level you can explain why Spartan women had unusual freedom.
summary: Spartan girls trained in athletics and Spartan women could inherit and own land and ran estates, unusual freedoms in Greece; they still had no vote, office or place in the assembly.

cards.headline: “Come back with your shield, or on it.”
cards.body: Later Greek writers put those words in the mouth of a Spartan mother sending her son to war. Legend or not, Spartan women had a reputation no other Greek women had.

cards.headline: Girls in training
cards.body: Spartan girls exercised like the boys: running, wrestling, throwing the discus and javelin. They weren’t trained for battle. Xenophon gives the reason: strong parents, Spartans believed, would have stronger children. So the freedom had a purpose, and the purpose was the army.

cards.headline: Owners and managers
cards.body: Spartan women could inherit and own land. And with the men so often away, they ran homes, farms and estates. Aristotle wrote that nearly two-fifths of Sparta’s land was owned by women, and he listed it among Sparta’s faults. He meant it as a complaint. Today it reads as one of the most surprising facts about the ancient Greek world.

cards.headline: Where the freedom stopped
cards.body: Spartan women still could not vote, hold public office or attend the citizens’ assembly. Freer than most Greek women, yes. Equal to Spartan men, no.

cards.fact: In 396 BCE a Spartan princess won at the Olympics.
cards.context: Cynisca’s team won the four-horse chariot race. Chariot victories went to the owner, so she became the first woman to win an Olympic victory without ever holding the reins.

cards.headline: Spartan women: unusually free

Women owned land and ran estates

questions.prompt: According to Aristotle, how much of Sparta’s land did women own?
questions.explanation: Aristotle wrote that nearly two-fifths of Sparta’s land was owned by women, and he criticized it.

questions.prompt: Which statement best sums up the position of Spartan women?

options.label: Freer than most Greek women, but without political rights
Equal to men in the assembly and the army
options.rationale: They could not vote or fight.

options.label: Kept indoors and barred from owning property
Rulers of Sparta in place of the kings

questions.explanation: Spartan women trained, owned land and ran estates, but could not vote, hold office or attend the assembly.

questions.prompt: Level 32’s men lived in barracks until about 30. What did that mean for Spartan women?

options.label: They lived in the barracks as well
They ran homes, farms and estates
They handed their land to the helots
options.rationale: Helots worked land; women owned it.

options.label: They moved to Athens for work

questions.explanation: With men so often away, Spartan women ran homes, farms and estates, and could own land themselves.
